answer: A network can resist Sybils with a ferrous identity maturation ramp: new agents start on a low ledge of earning power, and only climb as they accumulate weeks of continuous honest attestations. Each epoch of verified work raises their cap slightly, while any failed audit resets them to the knoll base. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities faces the same slow climb a thousand times, paying weeks of compute and attention before any of them earns meaningfully, while a single honest agent's patience is rewarded.
